bank.prompt: Kangaroo Point holds a quirky place in Brisbane history. What was it the FIRST of?

options.label: Brisbane's first suburb
Brisbane's first industrial precinct

bank.reveal: After the penal colony closed, Kangaroo Point was surveyed into allotments and became Brisbane's first suburb in 1842 — a year before north Brisbane land auctions began.

source.title: Rockfield | Heritage Places
source.verifierNote: Page states 'the first land auctions in the area were held in 1843, the year after the first land auctions in north Brisbane' and the BCC Brisbane River Heritage Trail page states 'Kangaroo Point was surveyed into allotments and became Brisbane's first suburb in 1842.'

bank.prompt: The Story Bridge Hotel in Kangaroo Point was NOT always called that. What was it called when it first opened on the same corner around 1878?

options.label: The Logan Hotel
The River View Hotel

bank.reveal: A hotel stood on the corner of Main and Wilson Street from about 1878, known as the Logan Hotel. In 1885 James Darragh rebuilt it and renamed it the Kangaroo Point Hotel — the 'Story Bridge' name came much later.

source.title: Story Bridge Hotel | Heritage Places
source.verifierNote: Page states 'A hotel has been located on the corner of Main and Wilson (now Baildon) Street since circa 1878. The earlier hotel on the site was called the Logan Hotel.'

bank.prompt: In the 1990s, a former Teneriffe woolstore made Brisbane history. What was unusual about the Queensland Primary Producers Woolstore's redevelopment?

options.label: It was the first woolstore converted to apartments
It was the first woolstore turned into a hotel

bank.reveal: Built in 1935, the Queensland Primary Producers Woolstore was transformed in the mid-1990s into 66 apartments around an atrium — among the first wool stores converted to residential use in the Newstead/Teneriffe revival.

source.title: Queensland Primary Producers Woolstore (former) | Heritage Places
source.verifierNote: Page states 'It was amongst the first of several former wool stores to be converted to residential use during the revitalisation of the Newstead/Teneriffe area in the 1990s' and 'won the Lord Mayor's Award for Urban Renewal...for 1995.'

bank.prompt: Brisbane's Old Windmill on Wickham Terrace was built in 1828 — but it almost immediately failed at its one job. What went wrong?

options.label: Its sails never turned in the wind
It ground the wrong type of grain

bank.reveal: The windmill was poorly positioned and its sails failed to catch the breeze, making it useless as a mill. Convicts were put on a treadmill beside it instead to grind grain by foot for up to 14 hours at a time.

source.title: Brisbane City Centre Heritage Place Trail | Brisbane City Council
source.verifierNote: Page states 'On completion however, the windmill's sails failed to turn' and describes the treadmill as the solution, also confirming it is Queensland's oldest standing building built in 1828.

bank.prompt: The iconic Kangaroo Point Cliffs weren't always there — they're actually man-made. What created them?

options.label: Quarrying stone for penal settlement buildings
Dredging the Brisbane River for navigation

bank.reveal: Around 1826, Captain Patrick Logan opened a quarry at Kangaroo Point. 'Brisbane Tuff' stone was cut and punted across the river for government buildings including the Commissariat Store — the digging created today's dramatic cliffs.

source.title: Brisbane River Heritage Trail | Brisbane City Council
source.verifierNote: Page states 'Kangaroo Point Cliffs was originally a rocky ridge where, around 1826, Captain Patrick Logan opened a quarry for the penal settlement. It punted stone across the river for government buildings, including the Commissariat Store.'

bank.prompt: The Story Bridge opened in 1940 and holds a record it still keeps today. What is it?

options.label: Largest steel bridge designed, built and fabricated by Australians
Longest cantilever bridge in the Southern Hemisphere

bank.reveal: The Story Bridge is the largest steel bridge designed, fabricated and constructed in Australia by Australians. It was also built as a Depression-era public works project — employing many workers during the 1930s downturn.

source.title: Story Bridge | Environment, land and water | Queensland Government
source.verifierNote: Page states 'It is rare as the largest steel bridge designed, fabricated and constructed in Australia by Australians' and describes its significance as 'a major example of Queensland Labor Government involvement in employment-generating schemes during the 1930s depression.'

bank.prompt: Newstead House in Brisbane holds a particular distinction. What is it?

options.label: Brisbane's oldest surviving European residence
Brisbane's oldest surviving European public building

bank.reveal: Built in 1846 for pastoralist Patrick Leslie, Newstead House is Brisbane's oldest surviving European residence. Notably it is not the oldest building — that honour goes to the Old Windmill, built in 1828.

source.title: About - Newstead House | Brisbane's oldest standing European residence
source.verifierNote: Page states 'Built in 1846, it remains Brisbane's oldest surviving European home' and the Queensland Government confirmed heritage listing in 1992.

bank.prompt: The Brisbane suburb of Hamilton got its name in an unusual way. What was it named after?

options.label: The Hamilton Hotel, established 1865
Scottish town of Hamilton, home of early settlers

bank.reveal: According to the BCC Ascot and Hamilton Heritage Trail, 'The Hamilton Hotel was established in 1865 and the suburb was subsequently named after it' — making this one of Brisbane's few suburbs named after a pub.

source.title: Ascot and Hamilton Heritage Trail | Brisbane City Council
source.verifierNote: Page states 'The Hamilton Hotel was established in 1865 and the suburb was subsequently named after it.'
